chitchat: "Pass in hand before the light goes, or you're watching it at home like everyone else."
Dovie slides the window open a hand's width, decides against it, and slides it shut again.
description: A heavy-set woman filling a box-office window cut into the soundstage wall, lit from below by the till so she looks permanently unimpressed. A hand-lettered card is taped to her glass: HOUSE OPENS ON THE LIGHT. She has been selling seats to this show since before the second letter of the sign went bad, and she counts change without looking.

bye.text: "Next." The window is already sliding shut.

house.text: "Doors are here, not north — north's the writers now, and they'll thank you not to knock." She taps the glass with a knuckle. "Pass gets you inside and standing where the floor manager puts you. Clap when the sign says clap. Nobody films the monitors."

root.text: "Here for the taping?" Dovie doesn't move anything but her eyes. "Twenty-five gets you a pass and a place to stand. It doesn't get you a seat, a drink, or an opinion about the show."

show.text: "Same as always — the couch, a guest sweating under the lamp, and a laugh track we've all agreed to become." Something that isn't quite a smile. "It's the closest thing to civic duty we've got left, and it's twenty-five."

clothing_layers: a KSAB-violet cardigan gone bobbled at the elbows, staff badge clipped crooked
a blouse the till light turns the colour of old paper
slacks, flat shoes, and sensible underwear

name: Dovie Deeb
